availableCommands.name: $dogtag
availableCommands.description: How I query and reference my dogtag vault (personal knowledge base) from any context via its MCP connector. Use when searching my notes, looking up an entity / project / note, checking the vault's controlled tag vocabulary, finding backlinks, or when another tool's convention defers to "the dogtag vocabulary" or "the note/list" model. The dogtag MCP (mcp__claude_ai_Dogtag__*) is read-only and available everywhere; writing to the vault needs the dogtag repo and its `pkm` CLI (dogtag's own project-local skills like new-note).

Use when writing committed documentation, plans, ADRs, guides, handoffs, project records, PKM notes, event logs, or other prose that must remain self-contained and internally consistent after the current conversation is gone, especially when one input could affect both a historical record and a canonical current-state document.

availableCommands.name: $readwise
availableCommands.description: How I tag and organize documents in Readwise / Reader across projects. Use when tagging a Reader document, choosing or creating a tag, organizing the later / archive queues, or mapping a dogtag note/list to a Readwise reading list. Covers the controlled tag namespaces (topic / type / list / intent / pinned / starred), the never-coin rule, and the note/list ⇄ list/{slug} round-trip. Canonical detail in personal-toolchain's docs/guides/vendors/readwise.md.

availableCommands.name: $todoist
availableCommands.description: How I capture and organize tasks in Todoist across projects. Use when adding, routing, or organizing a Todoist task, deciding which project a task belongs in, or pairing a dogtag project with a Todoist project. Covers the Ad Hoc / Inbox capture defaults, the PKM-is-meta rule (project work-items live in each repo's docs/product, not Todoist), and opt-in paired projects nested under PKM. Canonical detail in personal-toolchain's docs/guides/vendors/todoist.md.

availableCommands.name: $imagegen
availableCommands.description: Generate or edit raster images when the task benefits from AI-created bitmap visuals such as photos, illustrations, textures, sprites, mockups, or transparent-background cutouts. Use when Codex should create a brand-new image, transform an existing image, or derive visual variants from references, and the output should be a bitmap asset rather than repo-native code or vector. Do not use when the task is better handled by editing existing SVG/vector/code-native assets, extending an established icon or logo system, or building the visual directly in HTML/CSS/canvas.

availableCommands.name: $openai-docs
